rationale.complete: Round 1 done (71 units, 4 natives, synthetic validation, confirm script dry-run). Round 2 (pre-registered): content gate with H29's matched-age control (both embedding models, synthetic validation on the real skeleton), graph clause (pre-registered event study inconclusive, length bias diagnosed; post hoc relay RD), regime-I kernel with mixed-mode synthetic worlds and logged-start recipients; per_period_estimates rows; pair table for H67. Missing: HH188, agent impedance, the reserved-data run.
rationale.faithfulness: The gated-coupling model is identified and beats its rivals: read-out jump > 0 in 45/71 units and < 0 in none, onset exactly at hop 1, ungated coupling rejected, pure field rejected for talk, HH167's regime split rejected. The activity collective mode is shown to be a schedule field (edges explain ~0.6 beyond a shifted-input null; synchronous halts in #38). Not higher because the holdout is not run, the kernel shape was not predicted (plateau in III, rise in I), several numeric predictions failed (nudge onset, regime-I field share, corner frequency), and decomposition shares are model-based and non-additive. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F1 G1 H2 I1.
rationale.usefulness: A clean mechanistic decomposition operators can use: activity synchrony is the scheduler (stagger or trim before reading it as coordination); talk spreads one read-out call at a time, and in regime III only to named recipients. A diagnostic and design rule rather than a validated lever; calibrated 3.0 -> 2.5.

raters.claim: Scope: 71 non-holdout units (35 periods), ledger call times. Activity co-movement is mostly a scheduler field (daily start/stop explains ~0.6 of it), while talk co-movement is a coupling gated at the recipient's first read-out call (J1 > 0 in 45/71 units, none negative; onset at hop 1; zero at the in-flight call).
